--- page 1 ---
Main point: Cover/Executive Summary of the Bangladesh Monsoon Floods Anticipatory Action Framework, endorsed by RC 30 May 2021, pre-approved by ERC 3 June 2021.
No distinct figure/chart/map — narrative text describing the model (two-stage GloFAS/FFWC trigger), delivery, and money components. Key numbers: targets 410,000-440,000 people across 5 districts (Bogura, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Jamalpur, Sirajganj); ~130,000 more via additional financing; ~1 million via early warning messages. Stage I readiness trigger: GloFAS 15-day lead time, >50% likelihood of crossing 1-in-5-year return period at Bahadurabad over 3 consecutive days. Stage II action trigger: FFWC 5-day lead time water level crosses "Danger Level" + 0.85m, with GloFAS/RIMES showing sustained trend for ≥3 consecutive days. WFP/BDRCS cash: 78,000 households x 4,500 Taka (~US$53). FAO: 25,000 households (animal feed + storage). UNICEF: 110,000 people (water/hygiene).

- FAO: $773,284; 125,000 people; high-nutrient animal feed, waterproof storage silos.
- UNFPA: $711,397; 16,300 people; dignity kits, MHM kits, reproductive health kits, male condoms.

- WFP: $5,500,000 (incl. BDRCS sub-grant); 360,000 people; cash distribution; +65,000 additional reach.
- BDRCS: $431,932 (via WFP); 30,000 people; cash distribution, evacuation support, first aid; +21,000 additional reach.

TOTAL: $7,535,078; 410,000-440,000* people; +129,500 additional reach.

Table of Contents listing document sections (Executive Summary, Overview, The Model, The Delivery, Pre-agreed Financing, Learning, Final provisions, Annexes 1-6) with page numbers.

--- page 5 ---
Narrative text, no figure — "Overview and introduction": defines anticipatory action (3 core elements: model, delivery, money, plus learning), monsoon flooding context in Bangladesh (occurs March-Sept, peaks June-Sept, ~1/4 country flooded in average year, severe flood every 4-5 years), and past anticipatory action history (BDRCS piloted 2015/2017/2019, WFP 2019, FbF/A Technical Working Group established 2019).

--- page 6 ---
Narrative text, no figure — 2020 activation recap (triggered 4 July 2020, floods forecast from 18 July, 220,000+ people assisted). 2021 objectives: scale up to 410,000-440,000 people across 5 districts (Bogura, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Jamalpur, Sirajganj), ~1 million via early warning. Lists qualitative/quantitative scale-up priorities. Overarching framework: RC-led, anchored in existing coordination mechanisms (FbA/FbF).

--- page 7 ---
Narrative text, no figure — "The Model: Forecast and Triggers". Two forecasts used: 15-day probabilistic GloFAS model (T-15) and 5-day deterministic FFWC model (T-5). Severe shock defined as 1-in-5-year return period affecting >40% population and/or >20% household asset damage. Two-step trigger: Stage I readiness (GloFAS, 15-day lead, >50% likely to cross 1-in-5-yr return period over 3 consecutive days); Stage II action (FFWC 5-day lead crosses Danger Level (19.5m) + 0.85m, sustained ≥3 consecutive days per GloFAS/RIMES).

--- page 8 ---
Table: "Governance: Monitoring and activations" — Who/What/How/When.
- BDRCS-led forecast monitoring team (Hassan): monitors GLOFAS/FFWC forecasts twice daily, populates log sheet; from June 2021.
- Same team: confirms readiness and/or action trigger reached, related interventions can commence immediately; communicates via email/WhatsApp to RC/RCO, UN agencies, OCHA, partners, includes intervention map; as triggers are reached.
- CERF: sends approval letters when readiness (or action without prior readiness) trigger issued, based on pre-endorsed pilot and pre-approved CERF letter.
- RC/RCO: may call meeting with BDRCS working group, Red Cross/Red Crescent, BDRCS, WFP, FAO, UNFPA, UNICEF, OCHA, government (MoDMR) immediately after trigger; discusses coordination with government; as applicable.

--- page 9 ---
Table: "Improvements over 2020 — Readiness trigger skill level" comparing GloFAS model v2.2 vs v3.1 using ERA5 reanalysis 1987-2020 (7 historical action triggers).
Results 1987-2020 | Definition | v2.2 | v3.1
Successful pre-activations (readiness+action trigger): 2 → 4
False activations (readiness but no action trigger): 4 → 3
Missed activations (no readiness but action trigger): 5 → 3
Narrative notes v3.1 improves on all counts. Scenario probabilities: ~60% chance of correctly activating readiness trigger given a flood; ~40% chance readiness trigger fires with no flood within 30 days; ~40% chance action trigger fires without prior readiness trigger. Readiness lead time increased from 10 to 15 days with <5% increase in forecast error.

--- page 10 ---
Narrative text, no figure — continues improvements (no reduction in performance from 10 to 15-day lead time), known challenges (FFWC forecast negative bias/underprediction at longer lead times and high water levels; GloFAS-FFWC correlation has scatter especially at high water levels). Begins "The Delivery: Anticipatory Action Plan" overview — describes rationale for targeting at-risk populations distinct from in-need targeting.

--- page 11 ---
Narrative text, no figure — "Collective improvements for 2021": (1) joint targeting/common beneficiary database of ~100,000 pre-verified households across ~140 unions; (2) joint approach to early warning (WFP last-mile dissemination, FAO SMS blasts to 100,000 households with SGBV messaging from UNFPA, UNFPA integrates protection/MHM/maternal health messages, BDRCS last-mile warning + evacuation to 100,000 households).

--- page 12 ---
Narrative text, no figure — "Localization and collaboration with the government": ~20% of CERF financing sub-granted to local orgs (36% of total funding transferred to local partners), MoDMR Forecast Based Financing Task Force. Begins "Interventions by FAO": objective to protect livelihood assets of 25,000 households (125,000 individuals), reach 100,000 households with Early Warning Messages; high-nutrient animal feed to 12,500 households, waterproof storage silos to 12,500 households (typo "12,5000" in source).

--- page 13 ---
Narrative text, no figure — FAO-led anticipatory actions list (profiling, early warning, water-proof seed/food/storage silos, nutrient-enriched ruminant feed distribution, evaluation). Describes large ruminant feed and hermetically sealed storage drums procurement via private-sector Long-Term Agreements. Lessons from 2020 and 2021 improvements (cash+ packages, coordination with government/NGOs).

--- page 14 ---
Narrative text, no figure — FAO known challenges (start-up financing). "Interventions by UNFPA": objective to mitigate GBV, maternal deaths, menstrual health challenges. Key stats: 28% women of reproductive age, ~9,000 pregnant during monsoon period; only 53% of pregnant women access health-center births; maternal mortality ratio 165/100,000 live births; sexual violence prevalence among married women 13.3% (Rangpur 17.9%, Rajshahi 17.5%). UNFPA reach: >16,300 people; 9,150 women/girls/third gender with dignity/MHM kits, 3,800 pregnant women safe deliveries, 20 midwives trained (100 safe births), 1 health center upgraded (50+ rape cases capacity), 1,600 couples family planning supplies.

--- page 16 ---
Narrative text, no figure — UNFPA known challenges (pre-positioned stock lead time, COVID-19). "Interventions by UNICEF": objective — safe drinking water access to 110,000 people in Bogra, Sirajganj, Gaibandha, Kurigram, Jamalpur. Plan: 2 jerrycans (10L) + water purification tablets per household for 110,000 people; 10 mobile Water Treatment Plants at evacuation points for 2 weeks. Lists challenges (limited timeframe, duplication risk, COVID-19, <2% mobile plant failure rate) and way-forward bullet points.

WFP-led actions: 78,000 families targeted (72,000 via WFP + 6,000 via BDRCS sub-grant), one-off unconditional cash transfer of 4,500 Taka (US$53) via bKash. Plus 13,000 additional households via KOICA/GFFO/QFFD funds in Kurigram/Gaibandha.

--- page 18 ---
Narrative text, no figure — WFP lessons from 2020 (could not reach all beneficiaries, verification issues, only ~30% receive early communication). "Interventions by BDRCS": objective to reduce suffering via AA in Jamuna basin. Cash: 4,200 families via own FbA/DREF + 6,000 via CERF sub-granting through WFP; one-off cash transfer 4,500 Taka (~US$53) via Bangladesh Post Office. Non-cash: evacuation support (70 households evacuated last year), National Disaster Response Team, WATSAN team, first aid volunteers.

--- page 19 ---
Narrative text, no figure — BDRCS community engagement/radio show. "Interventions by Save the Children": funded outside CERF but same trigger mechanism. Focus: Sirajganj + Gaibandha districts, $350,000 total financing. Activities: unconditional cash grants, evacuation support via DMCs, pond netting support, WASH (shelter repair, hand-washing, water treatment, hygiene kits). Reach: Sirajgoni ~31,500 people (cash + WASH to subset of 11,250) + 225,000 indirect; Gaibanda 12,000 people (1,000 households) direct cash + WASH.

--- page 20 ---
Narrative text, no figure — Save the Children challenges (impact-based forecast gaps, 15-day resource mobilization). "Other AA projects to be aware of": SUFAL project (ECHO-funded, CARE/Concern/Islamic Relief/RIMES). "The Money: Pre-agreed Financing — CERF": ERC agreed up to $140 million globally for AA (as of 1 April 2021, $60M disbursed for Bangladesh/Ethiopia/Somalia pilots). For 2021 Bangladesh pilot, ERC allocated up to $7.5 million; pre-arranged for one severe flooding event over 2-year pilot period.

--- page 21 ---

Known challenges: lack of "start-up cost" financing.

WFP (CERF $5,500,000; Reach 78,000 households with BDRCS): activities and Stage I/II details (common database for 100,000 households, union selection via RCCC flood impact analysis + MoDMR + VAM, beneficiary selection/remote bKash verification, early warning via IVR/UDNMC, cash assistance to 78,000 households, 4,500 Taka via bKash).
